date_note: The page gives only its publication day (24 November 2026); the police warning is dated by it.
title: Styrian police warn of phishing after suspected data breaches at tourism bodies and hotel chains
geo_basis: Styrian police, as reported by ORF Steiermark
summary: Styrian police have recorded a rise in phishing messages sent by email, WhatsApp or SMS, ORF Steiermark reports. Police believe the senders obtained contact and booking details from suspected data breaches at tourism associations and hotel chains in recent weeks. The messages link to fake websites meant to capture payment and login details. The article names no organisations and gives no figures.
plain: Police in Styria say convincing phishing messages are rising. They think the senders got guests' booking details from suspected breaches at tourism associations and hotel chains.
exec: Police say suspected breaches at tourism bodies and hotel chains may be feeding convincing phishing aimed at guests.
action: Styrian police advise not opening links in suspicious messages, visiting the hotel or booking portal directly, and contacting your bank at once to block cards if you shared data.

validation.note: Only ORF Steiermark read, relaying the Styrian police warning; the underlying breaches are described by police as suspected.
